title: Congress hasn’t written AI’s rules yet. It already spends nine of every ten AI dollars with OpenAI.
excerpt: House records show OpenAI's ChatGPT took nine of every ten visible AI dollars in Congress, and Democrats, the loudest AI skeptics, spent the most.
content_html:
Before Congress writes a single rule for artificial intelligence, it has already picked a supplier. In the year to the end of March, House offices spent nine of every ten visible AI dollars on one product: OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

The figures come from a CNBC analysis of House disbursement records. Of $113,740 spent on named AI vendors, ChatGPT took $100,580, about 88% of the money and 96% of the transactions. Anthropic’s Claude was a distant second at $13,160. ChatGPT now appears in at least 71 member offices, roughly one in six.

The work is exactly what you would expect. Staffers use the tools to summarise bills, draft memos, prepare hearing materials and answer constituents. Representative Julie Fedorchak, a North Dakota Republican, said a ChatGPT-built database of her legislative work was “saving dozens and dozens of hours every week” of staff time.

The skeptics are the biggest buyers

The politics are the awkward part. Democratic offices spent $54,165 on identifiable AI tools, more than three times the $15,782 from Republicans. ChatGPT turned up in 44 Democratic offices and 27 Republican ones. That is the same party whose members have warned loudest about AI’s risks to workers, privacy and elections, now leading the spending on it.

None of this is neutral ground. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft are racing for influence across Washington as lawmakers decide how AI gets bought, used and regulated. The head start was structural. In 2023 the House handed out its first 40 ChatGPT licences, and by the time restrictions arrived in 2024 the name had stuck.

“ChatGPT was almost synonymous with AI,” said Marci Harris of the POPVOX Foundation, which trains congressional staff. She compared it to Kleenex and tissues, or Band-Aid and bandages. OpenAI reinforced the lead. It co-led training sessions for senior staff through a nonpartisan Hill group. It also spent $1m lobbying Washington in the first quarter, up 82.5% on a year earlier.

Why the vendor matters

Claude’s absence has a colder explanation than brand recognition. Interest in rivals rose only after Anthropic’s fight with the Pentagon, which named the company a supply-chain risk in March. The Senate bars Claude for official use outright. When your model is blocked, you do not show up in the spending records.

That is why the vendor question is not trivial. Eric Petry of the Brennan Center said the goal, “not to reward political favorites,” should be giving government the best tools available. His worry is that offices are standardising on one model before lawmakers understand how any of them behave.

The caveats are real, and CNBC names them. The records miss free accounts, AI folded into broader software like Microsoft Copilot, reimbursed purchases and almost all of the Senate. The true figure is certainly higher, and $113,740 is rounding error in a federal budget. What the numbers capture is not scale but habit.

And habit is the point. The same institution that will write the rules is learning what AI is from one company’s product. It learns on that company’s training, too. Meanwhile that company keeps tripling down on lobbying. Regulators tend to keep the tools they already know. OpenAI appears to understand that better than anyone.

content_html_zh:
在国会为人工智能制定单一规则之前，它已经选择了供应商。 截至 3 月底的一年中，众议院办公室将每 10 美元可见人工智能资金中的 9 美元花在了一个产品上：OpenAI 的 ChatGPT。

这些数据来自 CNBC 对众议院支出记录的分析。 在指定人工智能供应商花费的 113,740 美元中，ChatGPT 拿走了 100,580 美元，约占资金的 88% 和交易的 96%。 Anthropic 的 Claude 以 13,160 美元的成绩位列第二。 ChatGPT 现在至少出现在 71 个成员办公室中，大约占六分之一。

这项工作正是您所期望的。 工作人员使用这些工具来总结法案、起草备忘录、准备听证材料并回答选民的问题。 北达科他州共和党众议员 Julie Fedorchak 表示，ChatGPT 建立的立法工作数据库“每周节省了数十个小时”的工作人员时间。

怀疑论者是最大的买家

政治是尴尬的部分。 民主党办公室在可识别的人工智能工具上花费了 54,165 美元，是共和党办公室花费 15,782 美元的三倍多。 ChatGPT 出现在 44 个民主党办公室和 27 个共和党办公室中。 这个政党的成员对人工智能对工人、隐私和选举的风险发出了最强烈的警告，现在却在人工智能方面的支出领先。

这些都不是中立立场。 随着立法者决定如何购买、使用和监管人工智能，OpenAI、Anthropic、谷歌和微软正在华盛顿争夺影响力。 领先优势是结构性的。 2023 年，众议院发放了第一批 40 个 ChatGPT 许可证，到 2024 年限制到来时，这个名字就已经固定下来了。

“ChatGPT 几乎是人工智能的代名词，”培训国会工作人员的 POPVOX 基金会的马西·哈里斯 (Marci Harris) 说。 她将其比作面巾纸和纸巾，或者创可贴和绷带。 OpenAI 巩固了领先地位。 它通过无党派希尔团体共同领导了高级职员的培训课程。 第一季度它还花费了 100 万美元游说华盛顿，比去年同期增长了 82.5%。

为什么供应商很重要

克劳德的缺席有一个比品牌知名度更冷酷的解释。 在 Anthropic 与五角大楼发生争执之后，人们对竞争对手的兴趣才有所上升，五角大楼在 3 月份将该公司列为供应链风险。 参议院完全禁止克劳德用于官方用途。 当您的模型被屏蔽时，您不会出现在支出记录中。

这就是为什么供应商问题并非微不足道。 布伦南中心的埃里克·佩特里表示，“不是为了奖励政治宠儿”，目标应该是为政府提供最好的可用工具。 他担心的是，在立法者了解其中任何一个模型的行为之前，各办公室正在对一种模型进行标准化。

这些警告是真实存在的，CNBC 也指出了这些警告。 这些记录错过了免费帐户、人工智能融入到更广泛的软件（如 Microsoft Copilot）、报销购买以及几乎所有参议院。 真实数字肯定更高，113,740 美元是联邦预算中的舍入误差。 数字反映的不是规模而是习惯。

习惯才是重点。 制定规则的同一家机构正在从一家公司的产品中了解人工智能是什么。 它还从该公司的培训中学习。 与此同时，该公司不断加大游说力度。 监管机构倾向于保留他们已经知道的工具。 OpenAI 似乎比任何人都更了解这一点。
